{"kind":"finding","path":"/project/source/d.ts","line":2,"column":11,"severity":"error","rule":"@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars","messageId":"noUnusedVars","message":"'unused' is assigned a value and nothing ever reads it. A name that is written but never read is almost always the residue of an edit that moved on: an import whose call site was deleted, a parameter left behind when a signature changed, a variable holding a value nobody asked for. It costs nothing at runtime, which is what lets it accumulate, and it costs the next reader real time, because an unused name reads exactly like a used one until you search the file and find nothing. Delete it."}
{"kind":"finding","path":"/project/source/d.ts","line":3,"column":18,"severity":"error","rule":"eqeqeq","messageId":"unexpected","message":"This compares with `==`, which coerces its operands to a common type before comparing. That makes the comparison non-transitive, which is the one property every reader assumes a comparison has: `0 == '0'` and `'0' == []` disagree while `0 == []` is true. Write `===`, which compares without coercing."}
